prompt: How close can you park to a crosswalk?

decisions.prompt: You are parking at the curb before the crosswalk. How far back should your front bumper stop?

wrongActions.label: 5 feet back
wrongActions.consequence: Your car hid the crosswalk. A person stepped out from behind it and the next driver saw them only at the last moment.

wrongActions.label: 10 feet back
wrongActions.consequence: Your car hid the crosswalk. A person stepped out from behind it and the next driver saw them only at the last moment.

successText: You left the crosswalk in plain view. The person crossing and the next driver could see each other in good time.
ruleText: Do not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection: a parked car that close hides people who are about to cross. A few states set a different distance; add your state to the address to see its rule.

citation.source: Uniform Vehicle Code (2000), the model most state laws follow

verified: Read Nov 2026 in a hosted copy of the NCUTLO text: no parking "Within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection". California, Texas, Louisiana, New Hampshire, South Carolina and Oregon were checked and match; Wisconsin is 15 feet.
